findings.title: Upsampling eligibility check uses outer `dataset` instead of `scoped_dataset`
findings.body: Inside `_get_event_stats`, the call to `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)` uses the closure variable `dataset` (the request's top-level dataset), not `scoped_dataset` (the dataset actually being queried). The dashboard-widget discover-split logic calls `_get_event_stats` with `discover` as the scoped dataset and an error-only query (`AND !event.type:transaction`), but the eligibility check still evaluates against the original dataset (often metrics-enhanced performance), which `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns False for. Result: error-only split queries silently skip upsampling and return downsampled counts, producing inconsistent numbers between the split view and the direct errors view.

findings.title: `_is_error_focused_query` uses naive substring match on raw query string
findings.body: `if "event.type:error" in query` matches any occurrence of the substring, including negated filters like `!event.type:error` or `event.type:errorhabc`-style token prefixes, and it also ignores that the effective query can be rewritten by the caller (e.g. the endpoint's `(query) AND !event.type:transaction` split). A query that explicitly excludes errors (`!event.type:error`) will be treated as error-focused and have `count()` rewritten to `upsampled_count()`, which sums a `sample_weight` column that may not exist/apply, returning wrong counts or failing the query. The check should parse the actual filter AST rather than substring-match the raw string.

findings.title: `upsampled_count` SnQL function only registered on the discover dataset
findings.body: `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns True unconditionally when `dataset == errors`, and the endpoint then rewrites `count()` to `upsampled_count() as count`. But the `upsampled_count` function is only added to the discover dataset's `function_converter`. If the query actually runs against the errors dataset, the function is unregistered and the query builder will reject the column, breaking all errors-dataset stats queries for allowlisted projects. Either register the function on the errors dataset too, or never rewrite columns for that dataset.

findings.title: `upsampled_count` declares result type "number" while `count()` is "integer"
findings.body: The new function uses `default_result_type="number"` (a float) whereas the `count()` it replaces is `integer`. After the alias `as count`, API consumers (dashboards, alert thresholds, comparisons) receive floats like 10.0 instead of integers, and any downstream integer assertions/serialization of the `count` field changes shape. It should be `integer`, consistent with the alias it replaces (and with the `toInt64` wrapper already applied in the SnQL aggregate).

findings.title: Cache key uses Python `hash()` and per-combination project sets, making invalidation impossible
findings.body: The cache key is built from `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`. Beyond being needlessly opaque, the eligibility is cached per exact set of project IDs, so `invalidate_upsampling_cache(org, project_ids)` can only clear the one combination it is handed — removing a project from the allowlist leaves every other project-set combination stale for up to 60 seconds with no way to invalidate them. Additionally, `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is never called anywhere in the codebase, so allowlist changes never proactively invalidate anything. If a project is removed from the allowlist, its events (which may now lack valid `sample_weight`) will continue to be summed via `upsampled_count()` for the TTL, producing wrong counts. A versioned key or a short shared per-org key would make invalidation tractable.

findings.title: Tests mock `options` but not the eligibility cache, causing cross-test contamination
findings.body: The new tests patch `sentry.api.helpers.error_upsampling.options` but the real `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` also consults the shared Django cache keyed on org id + project ids with a 60s TTL. `test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects` caches eligibility=True for that org/project set; subsequent tests in the same run that mock `options.get` to a partial or empty allowlist will still read the cached True and take the upsampling path, inverting the assertions (e.g. `test_error_upsampling_with_partial_allowlist` and `test_error_upsampling_with_no_allowlisted_projects` expecting count==1 could see 10). The cache must be cleared or mocked per test, and the caching behavior itself is untested.

findings.title: Accidental nested `sentry-repo` gitlink/submodule committed
findings.body: The PR adds a `sentry-repo` gitlink pinning commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a. This appears to be an accidentally nested repository reference (likely from running tooling inside a checkout), not an intended submodule — there is no `.gitmodules` entry or description mention. It will confuse CI/checkout and should be removed from the commit.

findings.title: `store_event` factory unconditionally copies `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate` into top-level `sample_rate`
findings.body: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` runs for every `store_event` call, mutating `normalized_data["sample_rate"]` whenever the context is present. This changes event-processing behavior for all existing tests that (even accidentally) include an `error_sampling` context, and it silently swallows all exceptions with bare `except Exception: pass`, masking real shape errors (e.g. `contexts` being None yields AttributeError that is hidden). If this is only needed for the upsampling tests, it should be opt-in (a `store_event` kwarg) rather than a global side effect.
